---
title: "Proposal Overview"
---

## Summary

**Problem:** Drug shortages disrupt patient care and impose large costs on hospitals and
pharmacies. Warning time before a shortage is declared is highly variable, which makes
preparation expensive and difficult.

**Goal:** Determine whether shortage onset can be anticipated from public federal data, and if so,
identify which supply-side signals carry the advance warning. The project will produce a calibrated
probability that a given drug/route group enters shortage within a defined window, together with evidence
about which data features provide the signal.

**Unit of analysis.** Active ingredient per route of administration, for a total of 2,897 approved prescription
units.

**Validation.** Temporal only: train on earlier years, test on later ones.

## Planned Data Sources

| Dataset | Provider | Role | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|---|
| Archived CDER shortage CSVs | Internet Archive | Labels: onset and resolution dates | 102 captures, 2019–2026 |
| Drug Shortages (live) | openFDA | Current shortage state, NDC keys | 1,634 records |
| NSDE product lifecycle | openFDA | Supply-side panel; retains delisted products | 667,457 records |
| NDC Directory | openFDA | Product master, route and dosage form | 137,733 records |
| Drug Enforcement (recalls) | openFDA | Recall history | 17,899 records |
| Orange Book | FDA | Approval type, ANDA counts | 48,663 products |
| Medicare Part B / Part D | CMS | Demand, price trend, manufacturer counts | 15,335 rows |

All sources are US federal public-domain data, available as bulk downloads without
authentication. Total download is approximately 100 MB. The NDC product code is the primary join
key.

## Constraints and Challenges 

**The FDA live shortage data is only a snapshot.** FDA purges resolved shortages after
approximately six months post-shortage ending. Labels must be reconstructed from archived captures; this can be done from 
the Internet Archive, but
it introduces its own coverage limits (discussed below).

**Short shortages are under-represented.** The archived data has two gaps exceeding
FDA's purge window, and the median lag between a record's posting date and the first capture
containing it is 116 days. Episodes that open and close between captures are invisible. Both
effects bias the recovered record toward longer shortages, and we report this rather than
treating the panel as complete. In short: because of the available archive periods, and the 
6-month purge schedule, shorter shortages may fall through the cracks.

**Target leakage is a documented, severe risk on this task.** Any feature derived from how long a
record has been posted predicts the label almost perfectly while being useless in practice. We need to
identify a banned-feature list before modeling and treat unexpectedly high performance as a
leakage indicator until proven otherwise.

**The shortage causes are not stationary over time.** The FDA's attribution of shortage causes changes across periods, 
with some causes dominating during certain year ranges. Some of this could be driven by external environments (e.g. the COVID pandemic),
legislative/regulatory changes that require different reporting, or simply 'drift' from manufacters, as the causes are simply reported by
the manufacturers. Developing shortage-cause regimes thus may be a matter of temporal division, as well as cause-label grouping. 

**Licensing.** openFDA and CDER data are public domain and freely redistributable.

## Changes Since Milestone 0

The approved Milestone 0 proposal remains the basis of this project.

**Related/background work was identified and the contribution sharpened.** Two public GitHub projects
attempt a similar reconstruction. Neither is peer-reviewed and neither covers the full approved
prescription universe. The [Background](background.qmd) page states what they establish and where
this project differs: principally the full ingredient/route universe rather than using a WHO
Essential Medicines List subset, and the use of NSDE supply-side lifecycle data that neither
project employs.
